title: Strangers Pressed a 450-Volt Switch, Yet Refused One Direct Order
description:
In 1961 at Yale University, Stanley Milgram tested how far 40 ordinary New Haven men would press a 30-switch shock generator from 15 to 450 volts (Milgram 1963, Journal of Abnormal and Social Psychology). While 26 of 40 reached 450 volts in the baseline remote setup, archival and follow-up analyses (Haslam & Reicher 2012, PLoS Biology; Burger 2009, American Psychologist) revealed a critical twist: volunteers obeyed appeals to scientific duty, yet refused bare direct orders ('You have no other choice') and 90% defied authority when two peers stood up and quit.

Primary Peer-Reviewed Sources:
- Milgram S (1963) Behavioral study of obedience. Journal of Abnormal and Social Psychology 67(4): 371-378. https://doi.org/10.1037/h0040525
- Haslam SA, Reicher SD (2012) Contesting the 'nature' of conformity: What Milgram and Zimbardo's studies really show. PLoS Biology 10(11): e1001426. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pbio.1001426
- Burger JM (2009) Replicating Milgram: Would people still obey today? American Psychologist 64(1): 1-11. https://doi.org/10.1037/a0010932
